newsitem.title: UK: MARK CROSSES MIXED AMID UK, GERMAN RATE SPECULATION.
newsitem.headline: MARK CROSSES MIXED AMID UK, GERMAN RATE SPECULATION.

text.p: The mark was mostly steady against its crosses in quiet European morning trading, but the picture was mixed as speculation over British rates and German repo policy played with sentiment.

The mark was firmer against the lira but slightly weaker versus the French franc as players awaited the outcome of the Bank of England monetary policy meeting due at 1100 GMT amid speculation of a possible rate hike.
"The mark is fairly well bid on the EMS," said Neal Kimberley, EMS manager at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi in London.
"It's a steady market but there are no spectacular moves going on -- we're back in dollar mode again."
The dollar's surge against the mark, which took the U.S. currency to a fresh high of almost eight years on Wednesday, looked set to dominate play on Thursday, dealers said.
Dollar/mark was at 1.8815/20 at 0835 GMT, off Wednesday's peak of 1.8913 but up from 1.8808 at close of play in Europe.
Traders said dollar/mark could well attempt to break the key 1.90 level, which could pull the dollar higher against other EMS currencies and in turn support the mark on these crosses.

"As the dollar goes up people are buying dollars not just against marks but also against continental Europe," said Kimberley. "With the dollar going up, the mark should remain bid for choice in Europe."
